intent: To demonstrate that high-income earners face a higher effective tax rate than the ultra-wealthy, and that the ultra-wealthy's tax burden has decreased since 2001.

requirements.question: Must the video explicitly compare the 25% high-income rate against the 18.1% ultra-wealthy rate in 2008?
Must the video show the 2001-to-2008 decline in the 400 richest' effective tax rate?
Is the 25% high-income effective tax rate required as a standalone visible value?

units.claim: In 2008, the $100k-$200k income group's effective tax rate (25%) was higher than the 400 richest' rate (18.1%), a gap of 6.9 percentage points.

basis.note: effective tax rate for the middle income group
effective tax rate for top 400 richest tax returns

accept: 25% vs 18.1%; $100k-$200k earners paid a higher effective rate than the 400 richest in 2008
The 400 richest paid 18.1%, lower than the 25% paid by $100k-$200k earners
Middle/high-income earners faced a 6.9 percentage-point higher effective tax rate than the ultra-wealthy in 2008
units.evidence: Two 2008 values must be visible/labeled: $100k-$200k (or middle) at 25% and 400 richest at 18.1%, on a comparable scale or with explicit comparison labels.

units.claim: The 400 richest' effective tax rate declined from 23% in 2001 to 18.1% in 2008, a drop of 4.9 percentage points (about 21.3% lower relative to 2001).

basis.note: 2001 effective tax rate for top 400 richest tax returns
2008 effective tax rate for top 400 richest tax returns

accept: The 400 richest' effective tax rate fell from 23% in 2001 to 18.1% in 2008
The ultra-wealthy's rate declined by 4.9 percentage points since 2001
The top 400 rate was about 21% lower in 2008 than in 2001
units.evidence: Both top-400 values must be visible on a timeline or paired bars: 23% for 2001 and 18.1% for 2008, with a downward direction or change label.

units.claim: The $100k-$200k earners' effective tax rate in 2008 was 25%.

basis.note: effective tax rate for the $100k-$200k income group

accept: $100k-$200k earners faced a 25% effective tax rate in 2008
The $100k-$200k or middle-income group is shown at 25%
units.evidence: A bar/label for $100k-$200k or middle/high-income earners at 25% must be visible.

optional_valid: Highlight the 6.9 percentage-point gap between 25% and 18.1% as a derived comparison.
Show the 23% to 18.1% drop as an approximately 21.3% relative decline.
Frame the 400 richest' 18.1% as the lowest rate among the displayed groups in 2008.

g0_data_completeness.selection: all role=bar data rows; annotation rows excluded

clip_hardcase.reason: The reference SVG has no explicit data-role=bar mark, so visual-unit reconstruction needs manual review.

hardcases.handling: Requires human visual inspection before semantic scoring.
